subdivision_of_building: Internal areas , adding single storey rear extension.
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a Class C3 two-bedroom dwellinghouse to a Class C4 HMO for six persons represents a significant and harmful intensification of the site. The use of the property by six unrelated individuals would introduce a markedly higher level of activity than the lawful use, resulting in an over-intensification that would harm the character of the area. The principle of development is therefore considered unacceptable and contrary to Policies DMH 1, DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reasons of its increased number of independent occupiers, would generate materially greater noise, comings and goings, and garden use than the existing C3 dwelling, resulting in unacceptable disturbance to neighbouring residents. The submitted Noise Impact Assessment only assesses external environmental noise and does not address or mitigate the operational noise and activity associated with an intensified HMO use.The proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development provides no off street parking for a six person HMO, resulting in a full shortfall and increased overspill parking onto the public highway. Given the site's PTAL 1b rating, existing high parking demand, narrow carriageways and verge damage observed during the site visit, the development would exacerbate parking stress and create harmful highway and safety impacts. The submitted Transport Assessment relies solely on TRICS data and does not include a Lambeth methodology parking stress survey or any empirical evidence of local parking capacity. It has therefore not been demonstrated that the displaced parking can be safely accommodated on the surrounding highway network. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 116 of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed 6 bedroom HMO would fail to provide an acceptable standard of internal and external living accommodation for future occupiers. Bedroom 2 would suffer from an unacceptable loss of privacy and amenity due to its window directly adjoining the principal communal garden area with no defensible buffer, resulting in unavoidable overlooking and disturbance. Furthermore, the rear garden, measuring approximately 39sqm, would be significantly undersized for six independent adults and unable to provide functional, comfortable or usable external amenity space. As a result, the development would not deliver appropriate privacy, outlook or outdoor amenity, contrary to Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policies DMH 5, DMHB 16 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), and Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed cycle storage, due to its prominent siting within the open front garden, would appear visually intrusive and out of keeping with the established pattern of verdant, grassed frontages that characterise the surrounding streetscene. The introduction of multiple bicycles or an enclosed storage unit in this location would erode the openness and soft landscaped character of the area and fail to integrate with the local context. The proposal therefore results in harm to the character and appearance of the area, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and the design principles of the NPPF (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
description: Change of use from Class C3 (Dwellinghouse) to Class C4 (small HMO) for up to 6 persons including the erection of a single storey rear extension and cycle storage (amended description)

phasing_details.phase_detail: Internal refurbishment works, single storey rear extension.
